title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: Directors of the Company; Key Management Personnel (including the CEO, CFO and Company Secretary and their direct reports); any other person with authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the Company's activities; any person the Board designates in writing; and, for each of those persons, their spouse or de facto spouse, children under 18, financially dependent or acting-in-concert persons, and trusts/companies they or close family control or have an interest in.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Company; distinguished for clearance (approval from the Chair) and ASX/ASIC notification duties for changes in relevant interests.

tiers.name: Chair
tiers.description: The Chair of the Board; distinguished as the approver for other Designated Persons' and Directors' dealing requests and as the Approval Officer for Disposal Consent, while the Chair's own dealing requires prior written Board approval.

tiers.name: Employees, consultants or contractors (other than a Designated Person)
tiers.description: Staff who are not Designated Persons; may Deal in Company Securities at any time provided they do not possess Inside Information, with no Black-out Period, clearance, notification, hedging or margin loan restriction under this Policy.

definitions.hedging_definition: operate to limit the economic risk of any Designated Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including Company Securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under an incentive plan) on that Designated Person's behalf

windows.start_anchor: 7 days prior to the end of April, July, October or January
windows.end_anchor: business day after the release of the Company's relevant quarterly report

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to the release of the Company's half-year results
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after the release of the Company's half-year results

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to the release of the Company's full-year results
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after the release of the Company's full-year results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may impose, without notice and in its sole and absolute discretion, additional restrictions on Dealing by any or all Designated Persons, even outside a fixed Black-out Period; any such restriction must be kept strictly confidential. The Chair, in consultation with the Company Secretary, may also determine any other period to be a Black-out Period.

rules.detail: Company Securities is expressly defined to include options, warrants and derivatives linked to the underlying share price. Dealing (including entering an agreement to deal) in these requires the same prior written approval and post-trade notification as any other Dealing, and is barred during Black-out Periods or while holding Inside Information.
rules.evidence: Company Securities includes shares, options, warrants, derivatives and interests in shares (including vested options and vested performance share rights) linked in any way to the underlying price of shares in the Company.

rules.tier: Employees, consultants or contractors (other than a Designated Person)
rules.detail: This tier faces no Black-out Period, clearance, notification, hedging or margin loan restriction under the Policy; the only condition is not possessing Inside Information at the time of dealing.
rules.evidence: An employee, consultant or contractor (who is not a Designated Person) may, at any time, Deal in Company Securities if he or she does not have information that he or she knows, or ought reasonably to know, is Inside Information.

rules.detail: Protection arrangements, expressly including arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk of a security holding (e.g. hedging), are absolutely prohibited over unvested Company Securities, with no clearance route.
rules.evidence: The entering into of all types of "protection arrangements" for any Company Securities: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: Same absolute prohibition expressly extended to Company Securities that have vested but remain subject to a holding lock.
rules.evidence: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: For vested, unrestricted Company Securities, a protection arrangement that limits economic risk (including securities held beneficially in trust or under an incentive plan) requires prior written approval under clause 6.
rules.evidence: operate to limit the economic risk of any Designated Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including Company Securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under an incentive plan) on that Designated Person's behalf

rules.detail: Monetisation structures are not separately named but fall within the 'protection arrangements' prohibition, which is absolute over unvested Company Securities.
rules.evidence: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: Over vested, unrestricted Company Securities, a monetisation structure operating to limit economic risk falls within the protection arrangements catch-all and requires clause 6 approval.
rules.evidence: operate to limit the economic risk of any Designated Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including Company Securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under an incentive plan)

rules.detail: Short selling of Company Securities beyond the Designated Person's holding is expressly listed as a protection arrangement, absolutely prohibited over unvested securities.
rules.evidence: amount to "short selling" of Company Securities beyond the Designated Person's securities

rules.detail: Over vested, unrestricted securities, short selling as a protection arrangement requires prior written approval under clause 6.
rules.evidence: amount to "short selling" of Company Securities beyond the Designated Person's securities

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.

Contracts for difference are expressly named as a derivative market instrument caught by the absolute ban on short-term or speculative trading; a CFD used to limit economic risk would additionally be a protection arrangement under 7.3.
rules.evidence: This prohibition includes short term direct dealing in Company Securities as well as transactions in the derivative markets, involving exchange traded options, share warrants, contracts for difference, and other similar instruments, which are short term or speculative.

rules.detail: Absolute, unwaivable ban on entering into a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire Company Securities, with no clearance route referenced.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons may not: enter into a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities

rules.detail: Absolute ban on using Company Securities (vested or unvested) as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement.
rules.evidence: use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement.

rules.detail: 'Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement' is defined broadly (any lending arrangement using existing investments as security), so the ban reaches secured financing generally, not just formally-labelled margin loans.
rules.evidence: Margin Loan means any lending or similar arrangement allowing a person to borrow money to invest in securities using existing investments as security.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on short-term or speculative trading, not defined by a specific holding period or LIFO basis.
rules.evidence: Under no circumstances should Designated Persons engage in short-term or speculative trading in Company Securities.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within five business days of the Dealing occurring
clearance.evidence: Any Designated Person (other than a Director) wishing to Deal in Company Securities must obtain the prior written approval of the Chair or an Executive Director before doing so. ... any Designated Person who Deals in Company Securities must notify the Company Secretary in writing: of the details of the transaction within five business days of the Dealing occurring

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within five business days of the Dealing occurring
clearance.evidence: In the case of a Director, prior written approval to Deal in Company Securities must be obtained from the Chair.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within five business days of the Dealing occurring
clearance.evidence: If the Chair wishes to Deal in Company Securities, the Chair must obtain the prior written approval of the Board before doing so.

clearance.approver: Chair (Approval Officer), or the Board if the Designated Person is a Director
clearance.evidence: In exceptional circumstances a Designated Person may seek written approval from the Chair (Approval Officer) to dispose of or transfer (but not acquire or otherwise Deal with) Company Securities during a Black-out Period (Disposal Consent). ... may be made on such terms and conditions (including the duration of the right to dispose or transfer) as considered reasonable ... must be kept strictly confidential by the Designated Person

short_term.evidence: Under no circumstances should Designated Persons engage in short-term or speculative trading in Company Securities.

exceptions.evidence: transfer Company Securities already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Designated Person is a beneficiary

invest in, or trade in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in Company Securities) where the assets of the fund or scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party
undertake to accept, or accept, a takeover offer

participate in an offer or invitation made to all or most security holders, including a rights issue, equal access buy-back, security purchase plan or dividend or distribution reinvestment plan, where the timing and structure of the offer or invitation has been approved by the Board.

exercise (but not Deal with the Company Securities following exercise) an option or right under an employee incentive scheme where the final date for the exercise of the option or right falls during a Black-out Period
acquire Company securities under a bonus issue made to all holders of securities of the same class
acquire Company securities under a dividend reinvestment, or top-up plan that is available to all holders of securities of the same class

acquire, or agree to acquire, Company Securities under any employee incentive scheme or through the exercise of Company Securities under an employee incentive scheme (eg. options or convertible securities)
withdraw ordinary shares in the Company held on behalf of the Designated Person in an employee incentive scheme where the withdrawal is permitted by the rules of that plan

where the Designated Person is a trustee, trade in Company Securities by that trust, provided the Designated Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a Black-out Period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the Designated Person
the Designated Person is in severe financial hardship and a pressing financial commitment cannot be satisfied otherwise than by disposing of Company Securities

the Designated Person is required by a court order, or there are court enforceability undertakings, to transfer or dispose of Company Securities or there is some other overriding legal regulatory requirement for them to do so

external_documents: ASX Corporate Governance Principles and Recommendations
exemption_authority: Chair (Approval Officer) grants Disposal Consent to dispose of or transfer (not acquire or otherwise Deal with) Company Securities during a Black-out Period in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship or a court order/legal requirement); if the Designated Person is a Director, Disposal Consent may instead be sought from the Board. Decisions are made in absolute discretion without reasons, can be withdrawn if circumstances change, are final and binding, must be kept strictly confidential by the recipient, and may be made subject to terms and conditions including the duration of the disposal right.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin loan ban covers both acquisition financing and security
bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons may not: enter into a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities; or use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is barred twice over: a Designated Person may not borrow against Company Securities, nor use existing (vested or unvested) Company Securities as loan security, with no clearance or exceptional-circumstances route referenced for this clause.

bespoke_clauses.topic: Disposal Consent cannot override inside information
bespoke_clauses.clause: A person who possesses Inside Information is prohibited from trading and this applies even where ... Disposal Consent has been given under this Policy (whether in exceptional circumstances or otherwise).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a Board- or Chair-approved unwind or settlement of a collar cannot proceed if the director or executive holds Inside Information at the time.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any restriction communicated by the Company to any or all Designated Persons under this clause must be kept strictly confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An undisclosed ad hoc trading freeze can block execution, unwind or settlement of a collar at any time, including outside the fixed Black-out Periods.

bespoke_clauses.topic: protection arrangements reach beneficially held securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: including Company Securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under an incentive plan) on that Designated Person's behalf
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collared shares through a trust or custody structure does not avoid the hedging ban or the clause 6 clearance requirement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the order must be completed within five trading days otherwise it will lapse; and the order cannot be varied.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar leg placed as an order but not completed before a Black-out Period begins has only five trading days to complete unchanged, or it lapses entirely.

summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy. Clause 7.4 imposes an absolute, unwaivable ban on Designated Persons entering into a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire Company Securities, and on using Company Securities (vested or unvested) as security for such an arrangement, so the bank loan secured on the collared shares cannot be put in place. Independently, clause 7.3 bans 'protection arrangements' -- expressly including hedging, short selling, and profit-from-decrease arrangements -- outright over any unvested or holding-locked Company Securities, and requires prior written approval under clause 6 (from the Chair, an Executive Director, or the Board depending on tier) for the same arrangements over vested, unrestricted securities. Any dealing, cleared or not, remains barred while the person possesses Inside Information, and the Company may impose confidential ad hoc trading restrictions at any time, even outside the fixed Black-out Periods. Given the categorical margin loan ban in clause 7.4, the funded collar fails at the financing leg regardless of whether the derivative legs could otherwise be cleared.
